lane_impact: L10 persistence: the transcribe-don't-invent conclusion stands, but the range to transcribe is :2912-2930 (nineteen fields), not :2912-2925 (fourteen). Quest state and world location are in the shipped save format.
quote: :2926 'sharedObject.data.activeQuestList = StatsManager.getActiveQuestString();' :2927 'sharedObject.data.completedQuestList = StatsManager.getCompletedQuestString();' :2928 'sharedObject.data.playerlocation = StatsManager.getLocationString();' :2929 'sharedObject.data.taunt = StatsManager.getTaunt();' :2930 'sharedObject.data.friends = StatsManager.getFriendListString();' :2932 'sharedObject.flush();'
text: The offline SharedObject schema is bigger than the packet's persistence claim states. QueryManagerBase.as's offlineMode branch does not end at :2925 — it continues to :2930 and writes five more fields: activeQuestList (:2926), completedQuestList (:2927), playerlocation (:2928), taunt (:2929) and friends (:2930). Counting the fourteen at :2912-2925 plus these, the branch serialises NINETEEN fields to SharedObject.getLocal(cookieName + '_' + charname). A single-player persistence schema transcribed from :2912-2925 alone would silently drop the entire quest state, the player's world location, the taunt and the friend list — i.e. a reload would put the character back with no active or completed quests and no saved position.

lane_impact: L5 combat-core + L8: a seventh counted web-vs-android combat divergence. It hardens progression/player-stance-cycle-is-three for the TARGET build (three is right on web too, but for a different reason than that claim gives), and it supplies the stance-change gate a port needs: 48 reload ticks on web, not maxreload/6.
quote: web §1t99s0§.as:3060 'if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48)' :3064 'if(this.stance == -1)' :3068 'else if(this.stance == §1t12220s0§)' :3072 'else if(this.stance == §1t12221s0§)' :3076 'else if(this.stance == §1t12222s0§)' — no consoleEnabled test in the function || android MCSPlayer.as:2977 'if(this.reload < this.maxreload / 6)' :2981 'if(StatsManager.consoleEnabled)' :2993 'this.setStance(DUAL_STANCE);' :2997 'this.setStance(REVERSED_STANCE);'
text: The WEB v0.717 stance-change entry point is a different function from android's, in two ways nobody has claimed. Web §1t99s0§.as:3058-3081 (§1t4472s0§) gates on a HARD reload threshold — ':3060 if(this.§1t4414s0§ < 48) { return; }' — and then cycles only '-1 → Light', Light → Balanced, Balanced → Heavy, Heavy → Light. There is NO StatsManager.consoleEnabled branch anywhere in it, so the five-stance dev cycle (Dual and Reversed) that android MCSPlayer.as:2981-3002 exposes does not exist in the shipped web build at all. Android also gates differently: ':2977 if(this.reload < this.maxreload / 6) { return; }', which at android maxreload = 120 is 20 ticks, versus web's fixed 48 — and 48 is the same constant the web HUD subtracts in §1t113s0§.as:328, so on web the stance lock releases exactly when the focus bar starts moving.

lane_impact: combat-core + rebirth-elements: model the hit test as (horizontal broad-phase band of half-width dist) AND (per-part 2D overlap with the projectile clip). Implementing only the band makes every AoE hit airborne targets it should miss; implementing only a circle makes it miss grounded targets at range. The measured half-widths stand: Inferno 600 (BigFireBreathProjectile.as:32), Tsunami 400 (BigWaveProjectile.as:34), Tornado 200 (BigTornadoProjectile.as:33), Earthquake 50 (BigEarthquakeProjectile.as:68).

quote:
NPCManager.as:1444   if(enemydist * enemydist < distsq && enemy.checkHitObject(thing,damage,checkByAttacker))
NPC.as:323   public function checkHitObject(thing:MovieClip, damage:Damage, checkByAttacker:Boolean = false) : Boolean
NPC.as:326      var max:int = mcs.getPartListLength();
NPC.as:332      if(mc.hitTestObject(thing))
NPC.as:334         if(this.gotHit(mc,damage))
text: The AoE dist parameter is a broad-phase HORIZONTAL gate only; the actual hit requires a 2D bounding-box overlap. NPCManager.checkHitObject filters on |dx| < dist and then calls NPC.checkHitObject, which walks the MCS part list and requires mc.hitTestObject(thing). So an elemental ultimate does NOT have unbounded vertical reach -- an airborne or elevated target whose parts do not overlap the projectile clip is missed.

ledger_text: 1 what each element does (24 skills' damage/cost/AoE/status - names only).
text: A status effect and its duration ARE carried on the Damage object. launchType (constructor parameter 3) is the status channel -- Damage.STUN = 6, with isStun()/isDeathTouch()/isKnockDown()/isFly() reading it -- and setStunTime(num, stunPosX) writes a frame duration onto the same object. text: The 677-entry place-name table is byte-identical between builds: `cmp reference/extracted/bindata/98_1t4653s0.bin reference/extracted/android/89_NameGenerator_PlaceNames.bin` exits clean. This is a rare case where an S0-3 parity question is settled by a real byte-check rather than by the circular android-vs-android diff C2 warns about, because 98_1t4653s0.bin comes from the WEB bindata set and 89_* from the ANDROID extract.

lane_impact: L8 world-exploration: removes a plausible-looking porting trap. A reader diffing the two name generators would see a pool factory on the web side and suspect a different priming sequence; there is none. Combined with the byte-identical place-names blob, the ONLY web/android divergence in the whole name generator is the third Iwakuni override.
text: The web v0.717 RNG is pool-allocated rather than constructed - §1t136s0§.as:171 calls `§1t58s0§.§1t8804s0§(param1 * 2)` and then `.destroy()` - which looks like a divergence from android's `new RNG(territoryID * 2)`. It is not. §1t58s0§.as:23-27 gets a pooled instance and immediately calls setSeed (§1t779s0§), and §1t779s0§ at :67-74 sets the seed, takes its absolute value and primes with `this.rnd()` exactly as the android constructor does at RNG.as:10-19; rnd() at :84 is the same `(randomSeed * 9301 + 49297) % 233280`. Output is bit-identical, so any name-generator reproduction done against the android RNG is valid for v0.717.
